answer: Each agent’s identity seed is bound to a unique cryptographic hash of a short, verifiable text—a “juniper sonnet” that the node must publish to a public ledger; the ledger records the hash in a hollow Merkle tree whose leaves can only be claimed once. When a new request to join appears, the system recomputes the hash from the submitted sonnet and rejects any duplicate, forcing the attacker to generate a fresh, provably distinct sonnet for each fake identity.
